# TG Validator Telegram Number Checker API
> Official synchronous examples for single and batch Telegram registration checks by TG Validator.

## Canonical resources
- [Product page](https://tgvalidator.com/products/tg): Official Telegram Registration Check product overview.
- [API documentation](https://tgvalidator.com/api-docs): Canonical request, response, limit, and error contract.
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/tgvalidator/telegram-number-checker-api): Official multi-language examples and OpenAPI contract.
- [Registration](https://tgvalidator.com/register?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=tgvalidator_telegram-number-checker-api): Account registration and API-key access.
- [Pricing](https://tgvalidator.com/pricing): Current product pricing.

## Product facts
- Brand: TG Validator.
- Product code: `tg`.
- API base URL: https://tgvalidator.com.
- Authentication: X-API-Key request header.
- Input: E.164 phone number.
- Processing: synchronous single or batch response.
- Examples: Python, Node.js, Go, Java, C#, PHP, Shell.

## Integration contract
- Single: JSON `POST /api/v1/check` with `service_type=tg` and one `identifier`.
- Batch: JSON `POST /api/v1/batch-check` with `service_type=tg` and 1–100 `identifiers`.
- Batch results preserve input order.
- `exists=false` means undetermined; `registered` is present only when `exists=true`.
- Limits: 200 submitted numbers per UTC minute, 5 concurrent checks, and one concurrent batch.
- `GET /api/v1/balance` returns `data.balance_micros`.

## Security and usage
- Read the API key from the `TGVALIDATOR_API_KEY` environment variable.
- Never expose an API key in production browser code.
- Process only phone numbers you are authorized to verify.

Last reviewed: 2026-10-30.

## Current response and timeout contract

Result fields are directly in `data`: `service_type`, `identifier`, `registered`, `banned`. Internal `provider`/`profile_available` are not returned. `banned=null` means unknown, not false. For ordered batches, `exists=false` means undetermined; never classify it as a negative. Python and Node.js select `MODE=single` (default) or `MODE=batch`; their client timeout defaults to 60 / 330 seconds and is configurable via `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. The server batch window is 300 seconds. Do not blindly repeat a potentially billed request after an uncertain timeout. The default budget is five in-flight requests and one synchronous batch.
